title: Canonical coefficient direct-image mates: geometric and scalar coherence
statement:
Let $a:\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a map of commutative condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to W$ be morphisms of schemes with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and use ordinary uncompleted module derived categories. Write $T_Z=\Lambda'_Z\otimes^L_{\Lambda_Z}-$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change], $L_f=f_\Lambda^*$, $R_f=Rf_{*,\Lambda}$ and $L'_f=f_{\Lambda'}^*$, $R'_f=Rf_{*,\Lambda'}$, with their canonical derived adjunctions [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction]. Let $c_f:L'_fT_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}T_XL_f$ be the inverse of the canonical pullback comparison [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1). For $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ define
$$\gamma_{f,K}=R'_f(T_X\varepsilon_{f,K})\circ R'_f(c_{f,R_fK})\circ\eta'_{f,T_YR_fK}:T_YR_fK\longrightarrow R'_fT_XK.$$
Then $\gamma_f$ is natural in $K$, and under the canonical derived direct-image compositors,
$$\gamma_{gf,K}=R'_g(\gamma_{f,K})\circ\gamma_{g,R_fK}.$$
For $N\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ the unit and counit identities are
$$\gamma_{f,L_fN}\circ T_Y(\eta_{f,N})=R'_f(c_{f,N})\circ\eta'_{f,T_YN},$$
$$\varepsilon'_{f,T_XK}\circ L'_f(\gamma_{f,K})=T_X(\varepsilon_{f,K})\circ c_{f,R_fK}.$$
For a further map of commutative condensed rings $b:\Lambda'\to\Lambda''$, let $T_Z^a,T_Z^b,T_Z^{ba}$ be the three scalar functors and $s_Z:T_Z^bT_Z^a\xrightarrow{\sim}T_Z^{ba}$ their canonical derived tensor associator [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](3). The same counit construction satisfies
$$\gamma^{ba}_{f,K}\circ s_{Y,R_fK}=Rf_{*,\Lambda''}(s_{X,K})\circ\gamma^b_{f,T_X^aK}\circ T_Y^b(\gamma^a_{f,K}).$$
These are equalities of the specified module-derived morphisms, including the coefficient actions transported by the canonical Cartesian identifications [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. No flatness, boundedness, constructibility or invertibility of $\gamma_f$ is assumed.

proof.text: In [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] put $(L_1,R_1)=(L_f,R_f)$, $(L_2,R_2)=(L'_f,R'_f)$, $G=T_Y$, $H=T_X$, and $\alpha=c_f$. The two adjunctions exist by [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction], and $c_f$ is natural by [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1). The displayed formula defining $\gamma_{f,K}$ is exactly this mate formula. Thus it defines a natural transformation $T_YR_f\to R'_fT_X$ in the module-derived categories.

source.place: (2) Formal properties, first sentence: identify the specified map as the geometric-adjunction mate

proof.text: With precisely the substitution in step 1, [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility] at $N$ reads $\gamma_{f,L_fN}\circ T_Y(\eta_{f,N})=R'_f(c_{f,N})\circ\eta'_{f,T_YN}$. At $K$, [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] reads $\varepsilon'_{f,T_XK}\circ L'_f(\gamma_{f,K})=T_X(\varepsilon_{f,K})\circ c_{f,R_fK}$. These are the two required equations, with the actual units and counits of the specified adjunctions.

source.place: (2) Formal properties: compatibility with units and counits

proof.text: The general composable-scheme-map clause of [def-sfb-test-map-derived-composition] fixes the direct-image compositor $\mu^c:R_{gf}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_gR_f$ as the conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] of the pullback compositor $\mu:L_fL_g\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{gf}$, taken for the composite adjunction $L_fL_g\dashv R_gR_f$ and the adjunction for $gf$, for every commutative condensed ring; write $\mu'$, $\mu'^c$ for the same data over $\Lambda'$. Writing $\varphi=c^{-1}$ for the comparisons of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1), its composition clause $\varphi_{gf}\circ T_X\mu=\mu'T_W\circ(L'_f\varphi_g)\circ(\varphi_fL_g)$ inverts to $c_{gf}\circ(\mu'T_W)=(T_X\mu)\circ\delta$ with $\delta=(c_fL_g)\circ(L'_fc_g):L'_fL'_gT_W\to T_XL_fL_g$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2) with $L_1=L_g$, $L_3=L_f$, $L_2=L'_g$, $L_4=L'_f$, $G=T_W$, $H=T_Y$, $K=T_X$, $\alpha=c_g$, $\beta=c_f$: for the composite adjunctions, $\delta^\flat=(R'_g\gamma_f)\circ(\gamma_gR_f)$. Take mates of both sides of $c_{gf}\circ(\mu'T_W)=(T_X\mu)\circ\delta$ for the adjunctions $L_{gf}\dashv R_{gf}$ and $L'_fL'_g\dashv R'_gR'_f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](3)(a) with $\tau=\mu'$ the left side has mate $(\mu'^cT_X)\circ\gamma_{gf}$; by (3)(b) with $\sigma=\mu$ the right side has mate $\delta^\flat\circ(T_W\mu^c)$. Hence $\mu'^c_{T_XK}\circ\gamma_{gf,K}=R'_g(\gamma_{f,K})\circ\gamma_{g,R_fK}\circ T_W(\mu^c_K)$, which is the required equation under the canonical compositors.

source.place: (2) Formal properties: composition of geometric maps

proof.text:
Write $L^0_f,L^1_f,L^2_f$ for pullbacks over $\Lambda,\Lambda',\Lambda''$. Paste $c^a_f:L^1_fT^a_Y\to T^a_XL^0_f$ with $c^b_f:L^2_fT^b_Y\to T^b_XL^1_f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1), the mate of $d=(T^b_Xc^a_f)\circ(c^b_fT^a_Y)$ is $\delta_K=\gamma^b_{f,T^a_XK}\circ T^b_Y(\gamma^a_{f,K})$. Here all three geometric adjunctions are supplied by [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction]. Compatibility in [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](3), with the inverses of the comparisons in (1), says exactly
$$c^{ba}_f\circ L^2_f(s_Y)=(s_XL^0_f)\circ d.$$
In the defining mate formula from [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], precomposing a square by $L^2_f(s_Y)$ precomposes its mate at $K$ by $s_{Y,R_fK}$: this is naturality of the unit $\eta^2$ at $s_{Y,R_fK}$. Postcomposing a square by $s_XL^0_f$ postcomposes its mate by $R^2_f(s_{X,K})$: use $s_{X,K}\circ T^b_XT^a_X(\varepsilon_{f,K})=T^{ba}_X(\varepsilon_{f,K})\circ s_{X,L^0_fR_fK}$ and functoriality of $R^2_f$. Taking mates of the displayed equality therefore gives $\gamma^{ba}_{f,K}\circ s_{Y,R_fK}=R^2_f(s_{X,K})\circ\delta_K$, the stated scalar-composition equation.

source.place: (3), compatibility of successive scalar extension with pullback; direct-image proof Preservation, reduction to elementary maps

proof.text: Every calculation above takes place in the module categories and their ordinary derived categories: $T$ is the coefficient-extension functor of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change], and $c$ and $s$ are the specified module-derived isomorphisms of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback]. Whiskering and composing such morphisms retains their coefficient actions. The commutative coefficient squares in [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] identify the actions along geometric pullback and along $ba$; no equality was inferred merely after forgetting module structures. The mate identities used impose no invertibility of the mate, flatness, or cohomological bounds.
